correctness.rationale: The stated all-order run threshold is correct. Removing initial/terminal rotations and adjacent duplicate b's preserves synchronization and admissibility; on S={0,...,n−2}, ab is a cycle, so words without aa cannot reset. For m=n−1 the block aab(ab)^(m−1) sends each i<m−1 to i+1 and fixes m−1 (including m=2); repeating m−1 times after b works, has no aaa, and gives length 2n²−5n+3. An independently written exact backward search reproduced every length for 3≤n≤24 and replayed every stored word from every starting state. Each layer is a preimage of a terminal singleton under a suffix, with the suffix's leading a-run recorded. Prepending a uses inverse rotation and is forbidden at run two; prepending b forces membership of n−1 to match membership of 0 and resets the run. Empty preimages never grow, and first arrival at Q among the three run states proves the minimum. This verifies the finite formula, not an extrapolation of the frozen proof. The source's parenthetical assertion that every reachable subset is processed before Dijkstra terminates is unnecessary and not literally true: settling distances below the first singleton is sufficient.
